services.content:
## Branding & Graphic Design, with a clear purpose

A logo is one part of a brand. The useful work is connecting your positioning, message and visual language so a customer recognises you across a website, a presentation and a social post. We start with the audience and the role the identity needs to play, then build an agreed set of assets around it.

## What we can help with

We can develop a focused logo system, colour and typography guidance, reusable social templates, presentation graphics and campaign artwork. Each proposal identifies the formats, concepts, revision rounds and final source files. Existing brand assets can be refined instead of replaced when they already serve your business.

## How we check the work

You review creative directions in realistic uses, not just isolated mockups. Before handover, we check legibility, consistency, export sizes and how the system works at small sizes. Print production, licensed fonts and third-party imagery are agreed separately when needed.

services.seoDescription: Turn your footage into clear, engaging videos with considered pacing, captions, sound and motion graphics tailored to the channel.
services.content:
## Video Editing & Motion Graphics, with a clear purpose

A useful edit makes the message easier to follow. We work from your footage, script or content brief to build a clear opening, a coherent story and an appropriate next step. The format and viewing context shape the edit: a short reel needs a different pace from a product walkthrough or a long-form conversation.

## What we can help with

Projects can include short-form reels, YouTube edits, product explainers, interviews and simple motion graphics. We agree the source material, final duration, aspect ratios, caption language and number of versions. Editing uses supplied footage; filming, complex animation and additional production need a separate scope.

## How we check the work

Review links make it easy to give time-based feedback. Final checks cover caption accuracy, audio balance, safe text placement and platform export settings. You approve the work before publication. Music and footage rights must cover the intended use, especially paid advertising.

## Paid Advertising & Campaigns, with a clear purpose

An advertising account needs more than a budget. The offer, landing page, audience and tracking must work together. We begin with the action you want people to take and check whether the website can support it before scaling a campaign.

## What we can help with

Campaign work can cover Google Search, Meta and other agreed platforms, with account structure, audience planning, ad copy, creative testing and reporting. We define who owns the accounts, how spending is approved and what counts as a lead or conversion. The media budget is separate from management fees.

## How we check the work

We monitor delivery, spend and conversion quality, then change one meaningful part of the campaign at a time. Reports explain limitations such as consent gaps, attribution windows and low data volume. Results depend on the offer, market and budget; no fixed return is promised.

services.title: Technical SEO
services.description: Find and resolve technical barriers to crawling, indexing and a usable website, with priorities tied to your important pages.
services.seoDescription: Find and resolve technical barriers to crawling, indexing and a usable website, with priorities tied to your important pages.
services.content:
## Technical SEO, with a clear purpose

Technical SEO starts by understanding what should be visible in search. We compare the intended page structure with what crawlers can access and what Search Console reports. A prioritised plan separates issues that affect discovery from cosmetic scores that do not change the customer experience.

## What we can help with

Reviews can cover status codes, redirects, canonicals, robots directives, XML sitemaps, internal linking, rendered content, structured data and performance. Implementation depends on your platform and access. Large migrations, JavaScript rendering changes and infrastructure work receive a specific scope and rollback plan.

## How we check the work

We record the original issue, the change and the validation method. Crawl tests, rendered HTML and Search Console help confirm technical behaviour. Search engines choose whether and when to index a page; fixing a technical problem does not guarantee a ranking change.

deliverables: A handover showing remaining issues and monitoring steps

## Website Maintenance & Support, with a clear purpose

A website continues to change after launch. Content grows, dependencies update and business processes evolve. We begin with the current setup and agree a support boundary so routine care does not depend on last-minute guesswork.

## What we can help with

Support can include scheduled updates, backup checks, uptime review, small content changes and technical triage. We define included hours, response windows, access, supported systems and escalation contacts. New features, emergency recovery and third-party licence costs are listed separately where they fall outside the plan.

## How we check the work

A clear change log shows what was updated and checked. Riskier changes use a staging environment where available, with rollback planning and backup verification. Maintenance reduces avoidable problems but cannot remove every outage or security risk.

posts.title: SEO foundations that help the right clients find you
posts.description: A practical starting point for service businesses: search intent, useful pages, technical checks and meaningful measurement.
posts.content:
A service website has a specific job: help someone decide whether your business can solve their problem. Search visibility works best when it supports that decision. Before adding more articles, check whether your core pages explain what you do, who you help and how to take the next step.

## Start with the questions buyers ask
Write down the questions that appear in discovery calls. What does a project include? What affects the cost? How long can it take? What does your team need from the client? These questions are a useful starting point for research because they connect content to real purchase decisions.

A keyword is not a complete content brief. Look at the search results, the type of pages shown and the problem behind the query. A person comparing providers needs different information from someone learning a basic definition. Give each important service its own useful page instead of forcing unrelated services into a single paragraph.

## Make your service pages specific
Describe the deliverables, the working process and any constraints. Explain what a visitor can expect after contacting you. If you have permission to share a case study, document the starting point, work performed, measurement period and limitations. Avoid publishing outcome claims you cannot support.

Connect related pages with descriptive internal links. For example, a technical SEO article can link to your SEO service, while the service page can link to an explanation of an audit. The links should help a reader continue a task, not simply repeat a keyword.

## Check the technical basics
Open the site on a phone, test its forms and inspect important pages with Search Console. Confirm that public pages return useful HTML, have unique titles and can be discovered through navigation. Keep drafts and private business records out of search results.

Use a sitemap to describe the public URLs you want discovered. A sitemap is a discovery signal, not an indexing guarantee. Check canonical links, redirects and response codes after a migration so old links continue to lead somewhere useful.

## Measure inquiries as well as visits
More traffic is not automatically better traffic. Agree on what a qualified inquiry looks like and measure whether visitors reach the contact form, complete it and become relevant conversations. Compare changes across sensible time periods and account for seasonality and other marketing activity.

Search Console can show query impressions, clicks and average position. These measurements have limits: average position varies by query, country, device and date range. Treat the data as evidence to investigate, not a promise that everyone sees the same ranking.

## A manageable first month
Begin with a small audit, improve your most important service page and fix any broken conversion paths. Publish one genuinely useful supporting guide when you have something clear to explain. Review the results, collect new buyer questions and choose the next improvement from evidence.

Consistent, useful maintenance is more defensible than a high publishing volume with little original value. Search optimization should make the website better for the people you want to serve.

posts.title: Before you automate, find the work worth fixing
posts.description: Choose a first automation project with a clear owner, a measurable outcome and a safe path back to a person.
posts.content:
Automation is most useful when the task is already understood. A workflow that saves a few minutes hundreds of times can be a better starting point than a complicated system that tries to handle every situation.

## Map the current process
Choose a repeated task and document its trigger, inputs, decisions and output. Ask the people who perform it where work waits, where information goes missing and which exceptions require judgment. A simple process map often exposes improvements that do not require AI at all.

Lead routing is one example. A new inquiry may need validation, a service category, an owner and a follow-up reminder. The first version can be based on explicit rules. If natural-language classification adds value later, it can be introduced at that decision point.

## Choose a meaningful measure
Define the baseline before building. You might track response time, manual handling time or the number of records that require correction. Use a measure the team can observe consistently. Do not turn a model demonstration into a claim of financial savings without validating the real workflow.

Agree on the boundaries. Which actions may run automatically? Which require approval? Which data should never be sent to an external service? These are product decisions, and they shape the architecture.

## Design the exception path
An automation should not silently lose work. Log failures, retry temporary errors with limits and give the owner a way to inspect a failed job. Repeated actions need an idempotency strategy so a retry does not create duplicate invoices, messages or records.

For AI-assisted tasks, identify where uncertain output can cause harm. A draft summary may be low risk; an irreversible action based on that summary can be very different. Keep a person in the loop where judgment or approval matters.

## Start with a small pilot
Test with representative examples, including incomplete inputs and unusual cases. Compare the new process with the current one, collect feedback and adjust the scope. A pilot should produce enough evidence to decide whether to expand, change direction or stop.

Document who owns the workflow, how credentials are rotated and what happens when a connected service is unavailable. The person maintaining the system should not need to reverse-engineer its purpose.

## Build for ongoing ownership
A useful handover includes the process diagram, integration list, failure alerts, operating instructions and acceptance criteria. Review the workflow when business rules change. A working automation is a maintained business process, not a one-time installation.

posts.title: A better website starts with a clearer brief
posts.description: The decisions to make before design begins, from audience and content ownership to accessibility and launch criteria.
posts.content:
A good website brief makes the important decisions visible. It does not need to prescribe every design detail. Its job is to give the team a shared understanding of the audience, the outcome and the constraints.

## Describe the audience and their task
Start with the person visiting the site. What are they trying to do? What do they already know? What might make them hesitate? A buyer evaluating a specialist agency has different needs from a returning customer looking for support.

Choose the primary action for each important page. That might be requesting a proposal, exploring a service or reading a practical guide. The page structure should support that action with relevant information.

## Make content ownership explicit
Identify who supplies service descriptions, project evidence, photography and legal information. Decide who reviews the material and what approval means. Content often determines the schedule more than the number of pages does.

Separate verified claims from ideas that still need evidence. If a portfolio item is a concept, label it clearly. If results are available, include the measurement period and enough context for the reader to assess them.

## Agree on functional requirements
List the forms, integrations and internal workflows the site must support. Explain what should happen after someone submits an inquiry. Specify which team member receives it, where it is stored and how the visitor knows the submission succeeded.

For editable content, identify which fields the team needs to control. A useful CMS provides clear publication states and sensible validation. Giving every user unrestricted access is rarely necessary.

## Define quality and launch criteria
Include mobile usability, keyboard navigation, page speed, search metadata and browser support in acceptance criteria. Test real tasks on a small screen. Verify that contact forms work and that error messages explain the next step.

If an existing site is moving, prepare a URL map. Plan redirects for useful old pages, verify canonical links and check analytics after launch. Keep access to the previous content until the migration is confirmed.

## Plan the handover
Document hosting, domain ownership, backups, content editing and integration credentials. Assign responsibility for updates and incident response. The strongest launch plan includes what happens the following week, when real visitors begin using the site.

A clear brief reduces avoidable rework because it turns assumptions into decisions. Leave room for design exploration while making the business needs and quality expectations concrete.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.content:
## Information you choose to share
When you send an inquiry, we collect your name, email, company details if provided, service interests, budget range and message. We use this information to respond, assess project fit and manage the business relationship. Please do not send passwords, payment-card details or sensitive personal information through the contact form.

## Website measurement
Optional analytics are off until you accept them. When enabled, first-party measurement records page paths, event types and dates without a persistent visitor identifier. If Google Analytics is configured and you consent, Google processes analytics data according to its policies and your settings. You may change your choice using Cookie preferences in the footer.

## Service providers and transfers
Hosting and configured business tools may process information on our behalf. Access is limited to what is needed for the service. Providers may operate in other countries. The operator must assess applicable transfer requirements before activating a provider. We do not sell inquiry information.

## Retention and security
We retain inquiries while they are needed to respond, manage a relationship or meet legal obligations. Analytics events are deleted according to the configured retention period, which defaults to 90 days. Administrative access is protected and credentials are kept on the server. No internet service can promise absolute security.

## Your choices
You can request access, correction or deletion of your inquiry information through our Contact page. Rights and exceptions depend on applicable law. Identify the email address used in your inquiry so we can verify the request.

## Contact and changes
Growintek is the website operator. Use the Contact page for privacy questions. This policy was prepared on 31 October 2026 and should be reviewed whenever processing practices or operator details change.

## Blog comments

When you submit a comment, we store your name, email address, comment and confirmation that you follow our social profiles. Your name and comment become public only after approval. Your email is visible only to website administrators and is used to manage the comment. Social follows are self-confirmed, not verified through social-platform accounts. Opening a profile takes you to that platform, where its own privacy practices apply. Contact us to request removal of your comment or associated personal information.
pages.description: Growintek privacy policy: how we operate and how to contact us.

pages.title: Terms of Use
pages.content:
## Using this website
This website describes Growintek services and provides general educational information. Content does not constitute a binding offer, legal advice or a guarantee of business results. Do not misuse the website, attempt unauthorized access or interfere with its operation.

## Project agreements
Scope, delivery dates, fees, payment terms, intellectual property rights and support obligations are agreed in a separate written project agreement. Sending an inquiry does not create a client relationship or reserve delivery capacity.

## Intellectual property
Website copy, design and original materials belong to their respective rights holders. You may share links and use the site for legitimate evaluation. Reproduction or commercial reuse beyond applicable legal exceptions requires permission.

## Portfolio and performance
Concept work is labeled as such. Outcomes depend on project scope, market conditions, client participation and third-party platforms. We do not guarantee rankings, traffic, revenue, indexing or advertising performance.

## External services
Linked platforms and optional social embeds operate under their own terms and policies. Their availability is outside our control.

## Availability and liability
We take reasonable steps to maintain accurate content and reliable access. The website may contain errors or become unavailable. Any limitation of liability applies only to the extent permitted by applicable law and does not exclude rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.

## Questions
Contact Growintek through the Contact page. Specific governing-law and dispute-resolution terms should be set in the signed project agreement. Last updated 31 October 2026.

## Comment guidelines

Comments should be relevant, respectful and useful. Links, web addresses, markup, promotional messages and abusive content are not allowed. Submitting requires your confirmation that you follow the listed Growintek profiles. Opening a link does not verify a follow. All comments are moderated; we may decline or remove comments that do not meet these guidelines. Do not include confidential information or someone else’s personal details.
pages.description: Growintek terms of use: how we operate and how to contact us.

pages.title: Cookie Policy
pages.content:
## Essential storage
The public site stores your cookie preferences in your browser. The admin area uses an essential, HTTP-only session cookie named grow_session to keep authorized administrators signed in. That cookie expires after eight hours.

## Optional analytics
Analytics remain disabled until you choose Accept analytics. If configured, Google Analytics may set cookies for measurement. First-party events record page paths and dates without a persistent visitor identifier. Choosing Reject optional keeps these features off.

## Social content
Social video players and external embeds are loaded only after a separate action to enable external media. They may transmit your IP address and browser information to the provider and may use their own storage. Links to social platforms do not load embedded feeds by themselves.

## Changing your choice
Open Cookie preferences in the footer at any time. Withdrawing consent disables future analytics collection and removes accessible Google Analytics cookies; the page reloads to stop loaded third-party scripts. Your browser also lets you delete stored information.

## Contact
Use our Contact page for questions about cookies or tracking. Last updated 31 October 2026.
pages.description: Growintek cookie policy: how we operate and how to contact us.

pages.title: Accessibility Statement
pages.content:
## Our approach
We aim to make Growintek usable across devices and input methods. The site includes keyboard-accessible navigation, visible focus indicators, labeled form controls, reduced-motion support and descriptive page structure.

## Ongoing improvement
Accessibility is a continuing process. New content and third-party services can introduce issues. We review important journeys, including service discovery and contact, as the site changes.

## Report a barrier
If you have difficulty using the site, please contact us with the page, the task you were trying to complete and any relevant assistive technology details. Avoid including sensitive information. We will use the report to investigate and improve the experience.
pages.description: Growintek accessibility statement: how we operate and how to contact us.

pages.title: Editorial & AI Policy
pages.content:
## Useful, accountable content
Our editorial goal is to answer real business questions with clear, practical information. We distinguish general guidance, design concepts and verified project evidence. We do not fabricate experience, credentials, sources or performance results.

## AI assistance
AI may help develop outlines or drafts. AI-assisted posts are identified on their article pages. Articles may publish after automated source, format and duplication checks under our selected publishing settings. These articles disclose when no human review has taken place. An editor can also review and correct an article before or after publication. Automated checks cannot replace professional judgment.

## Sources and corrections
Sources are listed where they support a technical or factual claim. Editors should verify references and remove unsupported claims. If you notice an error, contact us with the article URL and the correction you believe is needed.

## Search practices
We use descriptive content, technical improvements and accessible design to support discovery. We do not use cloaking, link schemes, keyword stuffing, fake reviews or mass publication designed only to manipulate rankings. Search engines decide what to index and rank.
